introduction: On this third Sunday of Lent, the thirsty Israelites complain in the desert, and God gives them water from the rock. In the Gospel, Jesus meets a Samaritan woman at a well and offers her living water, welling up to eternal life. Paul tells us that God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit. Today, where catechumens celebrate the first scrutiny, we pray for them as they prepare for Baptism.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God's love has been poured into our hearts. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may lead all who are thirsty to Christ, the source of living water. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the catechumens: that Christ may free them from all that holds them back and fill them with his Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who lack clean water, and for all who thirst: that their needs may be met. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who carry hidden shame: that, like the Samaritan woman, they may meet Christ who knows them and loves them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may worship the Father in spirit and truth. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you gave water from the rock and your Son offers living water to all who thirst. Fill us with your Spirit, and lead the catechumens to the waters of Baptism. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Living water
reflection.body:
In the desert, the people are thirsty, and their thirst turns into doubt: "Is the LORD among us, or not?" God answers by telling Moses to strike the rock, and water flows out. The psalm remembers that place and warns us: "Today, oh that you would hear his voice! Don't harden your heart, as at Meribah."

In the Gospel, Jesus is tired from his journey and sits by Jacob's well at noon. A Samaritan woman comes to draw water, alone, at the hottest time of day. Jesus asks her, "Give me a drink." She is surprised: Jews and Samaritans did not mix, and men did not usually speak with women they did not know.

Jesus begins to speak of a different kind of water: "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you," Give me a drink, "you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water." Ordinary water satisfies only for a while, "but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again."

Then Jesus gently brings her own life into the light. He knows about her five husbands and the man she now lives with. He does not condemn her. He reveals himself to her: "I am he, the one who speaks to you." She leaves her water jar and runs to tell the town: "Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done. Can this be the Christ?" The woman who came alone becomes the first missionary to her people.

Paul tells us what this living water is: "God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us."

Today the Church prays for catechumens preparing for Baptism. This week, bring your own thirst to Jesus: for meaning, for forgiveness, for love. Let him know you completely, and receive his living water.
